question:
Computer Graphics & Game Development

A light source at $L(6,4,-1)$ is reflected in plane $3x-4y+2z=10$.

(1) Find the coordinates of the reflected image.

(2) Find direction cosines of the line joining source and image.

(3) Show this line is perpendicular to the plane.

(4) Explain relevance to ray tracing.
explanation:
Normal $(3,-4,2)$.

Normal line through $L$: $x=6+3t$, $y=4-4t$, $z=-1+2t$.

Substituting into plane gives $t=10/29$.

Foot $F(204/29,76/29,-9/29)$.

Using midpoint relation gives image $L'(236/29,36/29,11/29)$.

Direction vector from $L$ to $L'$ proportional to $(3,-4,2)$, same as plane normal.

Hence line joining them is perpendicular to plane.

This ensures accurate reflection calculation in ray-tracing graphics engines.

options.A:
(1) Reflected image is $L'\left(\frac{234}{29},\frac{36}{29},\frac{11}{29}\right)$
(2) Direction cosines are $\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{29}},\frac{-4}{\sqrt{29}},\frac{2}{\sqrt{29}}\right)$
(3) The joining line is parallel to normal $(3,-4,2)$, hence perpendicular to the plane
(4) This is used for accurate reflection in ray tracing
options.B:
(1) Reflected image is $L'\left(\frac{236}{29},\frac{36}{29},\frac{11}{29}\right)$
(2) Direction cosines are $\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{29}},\frac{-4}{\sqrt{29}},\frac{3}{\sqrt{29}}\right)$
(3) The line is parallel to the plane
(4) This gives diffuse lighting only
options.C:
(1) Reflected image is $L'\left(\frac{204}{29},\frac{76}{29},\frac{-9}{29}\right)$
(2) Direction cosines are $\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{29}},\frac{-4}{\sqrt{29}},\frac{2}{\sqrt{29}}\right)$
(3) The line lies in the plane
(4) This gives only the foot of perpendicular
options.D:
(1) Reflected image is $L'(6,4,-1)$
(2) Direction cosines are $(0,0,0)$
(3) The line is undefined
(4) Reflection does not change the source point
